distractors.reason: We don't say 'much expensive'. 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns or with comparatives, such as 'much more expensive'.
'Many' is used with plural countable nouns, such as 'many shops'. It does not modify an adjective like 'expensive'.
'Big' is an adjective, not an adverb, so it cannot modify another adjective. We don't say 'big expensive'.

example_sentence: The jacket in this shop is ___ expensive, so I cannot buy it.
l1_interference: Polish speakers may translate 'dużo drogi' literally and say 'much expensive', because 'dużo' means 'much' or 'a lot'. In English, we use 'very' before an adjective like 'expensive'.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the most common degree adverb for making an adjective stronger. Learn 'very expensive' as a fixed pair, because 'much' does not work in this position.

related_collocations.example: These socks are very cheap, so I will buy three pairs.
The museum is completely free on Sundays.
This shopping list is really useful.

memory_tip: VERY + adjective = strong degree (very cheap, very expensive) | MUCH + comparative = more (much more expensive)
